items.title: Reconcile this backlog with current source and active work
items.problem: Plans and implementation evidence are spread across files; the captured source can change while other tasks work.
scope: Existing roadmap, execution status, open issues and pull requests (read-only)
acceptance: Classify each candidate as implemented, still open, superseded or awaiting evidence; retain source links and reasons.
Inspect dirty state, remotes, worktrees and local environment presence without reading secrets; avoid duplicate work with active owners.
Resolve the actual offline validation commands and record exact current default-branch/working-tree provenance; do not copy historical live passes to newer code.
validation: Read the applicable instructions and validation workflow; read gh issue list and gh pr list for the named repository using nathanmcnulty. Do not create or modify issues/PRs.
evidence: 2026-10-04 read-only reconciliation against current main 859d4ca38e456964e297250fdcd3c0f19c7dff21: inspected canonical dirty state, remotes, worktrees and environment-path presence without reading values; active/unowned branches remain untouched. Reviewed current issue/PR inventory, roadmap/TODO task sources and .github/workflows/validate.yml; kept live and optional-feature gates proposed.

Invoke-Pester ./tests -CI: 113/113 passed, including missing/mismatched Azure tenant binding cases. Validation used offline fixtures only; no cloud, tenant, recipient or endpoint action was performed.

items.title: Qualify the read-only readiness and exact-feature pilot
items.problem: Licensing, connectors, cloud support and Graph beta mutations remain feature-specific gates.
acceptance: Record readiness, connector health and stale-plan rejection before authorizing one named feature.
Test exact-ID rollback and reused-object preservation for that feature.
TLS, forwarding, remote networks, CA and Intune assignments remain independent approvals with no broadened scope.
validation: Use the offline commands in the registered validation workflow; record the exact commands, revision and results before implementation is complete.
Run focused tests for changed behavior from tests/; fixtures do not prove live-service or endpoint behavior.
After separate authorization, retain redacted exact-target live evidence and cleanup results outside public Git. Do not execute live operations from this backlog alone.

items.title: Evaluate shared auth/validation and CRL health reporting
items.problem: Graph session reuse and optional TLS/CRL state can be represented consistently without sharing policy mutation logic.
acceptance: Compare delegated Graph coordinator only with a compatible Microsoft.Graph.Authentication session; do not replace unrelated Azure CLI flows.
Report exact target/licensing/connector and optional CRL expiry status using bounded validation.
TLS renewal or central alert sending is never executed by a read-only health check.
validation: Use the offline commands in the registered validation workflow; record the exact commands, revision and results before implementation is complete.
Run focused tests for changed behavior from tests/; fixtures do not prove live-service or endpoint behavior.
evidence: Partial CRL correctness/privacy improvement: publication verification derives from validated committed and downloaded SHA-256 fingerprints, ignoring caller hashMatches. CRL DTOs omit URL/provider errors/unknown fields. Legacy nextUpdate remains normalized committed metadata with nextUpdateSource=committedState; observedNextUpdate is null and expiryObserved=false. Recorded expired/near dates retain Fail/Warning; future recorded dates remain advisory Warning, not observed-expiry Pass. Other readiness DTOs and ready=no-Fail semantics, public HTTP CDP, renewal/auth/infra/defaults remain unchanged. A minimal adjacent array normalization preserves empty Internet-baseline results so readiness reaches the CRL check. PowerShell 7.6.6 full141 tests/28 new cases, analyzer Error+Warning, parse/Bicep/package/local azd-load gates pass; no live readiness/renewal/grant/alert execution.

Bounded CRL transport closes the selected GSA-003 download gap: the read-only entrypoint uses one direct anonymous no-redirect HttpClient request with ambient proxies disabled, a 15-second total header/body deadline and 1 MiB streaming limit. Only a complete nonempty HTTP 200 application/pkix-crl body is hashed; malformed or credential-bearing locations, redirects, invalid media/status, oversized, truncated and timed-out bodies fail to the existing closed DTO without URL or provider error details. Focused PowerShell 7.6.6 tests pass 44/44, including real loopback transport, credentialed ambient-proxy bypass and actual entrypoint wiring, and changed production scripts pass PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 Error+Warning with zero findings. Public HTTP CDP, renewal, publication, auth, infrastructure and defaults remain unchanged; no live readiness/renewal/grant/alert execution occurred. GSA-003 remains proposed because its broader authentication, target, licensing and connector acceptance is not closed.

Bounded Graph pagination closes the selected GSA-003 continuation gap: every initial and continuation location is bound to the current known Graph cloud HTTPS origin and exact collection path before dispatch, opaque locations and caller headers are forwarded unchanged, malformed collection envelopes, cycles and malformed links fail closed, and complete results are buffered behind default 100-page/10,000-item limits with declared override maxima. All 35 production call sites use collection endpoints, so non-collection response fallback was removed. Focused PowerShell 7.6.6 Common+Graph tests pass 55/55 and changed production code passes PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0 Error+Warning with zero findings. The graph-delegated-authentication 0.1.1 comparison is pinned to azd-reference revision d4d2fee7440b2dc700d2e7898cc0c932b9300314; its explicit tenant/account/probe/interaction contract remains separate unresolved work. No authentication, consent, scope, SDK retry/timeout, mutation or runtime dependency changed, and no live Graph request occurred. GSA-003 remains proposed.

Explicit Graph tenant binding closes the selected GSA-003 target-selection gap: all six callers supply an existing configured or committed tenant, and Connect-GsaGraph validates a nonzero tenant GUID before reading context. A cached context is reused only for the same tenant and cloud; mismatch fails before login, consent or Graph reads. Normal browser authentication receives the normalized target tenant GUID when context or scopes are absent, followed by tenant, cloud and scope verification. Readiness records Fail and performs no Graph interaction for a missing or malformed AZURE_TENANT_ID instead of claiming tenant consistency. Focused PowerShell 7.6.6 tenant/Common/CRL entrypoint and transport tests pass 114/114. Post-provision now rejects a configured subscription or tenant mismatch against Azure CLI before Graph connection or scope consent, while retaining the post-connect Graph tenant comparison; focused ordering tests pass 24/24 with zero Graph connects or dispatches for both mismatch cases. Existing manifest and subscription guards remain, no scopes or SDK dependencies changed, and no live login, consent, probe, Graph read or mutation occurred. Broader expected-account and probe qualification remains open, so GSA-003 remains proposed.
